propositions: Hand-rolled CLI argument parsing loops in claim.py and transition.py must be replaced with stdlib argparse while preserving all observable behavior and None-vs-empty-string sentinel semantics.

The --force flag has command-specific semantics: claim bare --force consumes next non-option token as reason else '(no reason given)', while transition bare --force sets force_reason='' (not consuming following tokens) with observable note '(no reason given)' via _force_note().
The --assignee flag must preserve None-vs-'' distinction (absent → default_assignee fallback, explicit '' → cleared) and reject value-less invocations with exit code 1.

The --help output is dispatcher-served byte-exact from golden files (help/claim.txt, help/transition.txt) pinned by tests; argparse must not regenerate help (add_help=False, parse_known_args for unknown-token skip).

Direct external callers of transition._parse_flags must continue to receive identical 5-tuple (reason, force_reason, close_class, caused_by, ref) with retired --force-close rejected via exit-1; three tests (test_close_ref_target_80af.py, test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py, test_dependency_audit.py) verify this.

Code complexity and module size ratchets must be maintained (transition ≤800 LOC, _parse_flags dropped below ceiling); argparse-backed WriteArgParser/write_arg_parser() shared in _seam.py with CommandError(returncode=1) error override for historical message fidelity.
